# PackageContentSetup

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.Setup` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Setup/PackageContentSetup.cs#L22)

The parts of the setup that bring content in from outside the project: packages the framework
depends on but does not ship, the TextMesh Pro resources, and the XR samples the framework's
prefabs are built on.
All three make Unity recompile, which is what used to break a single-pass setup and forced the
old "run this menu item, then that one" split. [`SetupRunner`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/SetupRunner) handles the reloads;
the work here only has to say when it is finished.


## Methods

### AddRequiredPackages() {#addrequiredpackages}

Installs whatever required package is not in the project yet. One request for all of them,
so the package manager resolves and reloads once instead of once per package.

```csharp
public static void AddRequiredPackages()
```

### AllowPreReleasePackages() {#allowprereleasepackages}

Ticks "Enable Pre-release Packages" in Project Settings > Package Manager.

Not a preference the setup is helping itself to: `com.unity.ai.assistant`, which
brings Unity's MCP bridge, has never published anything but pre-releases. With this
off, the package manager will not resolve it at all and every step that depends on the
editor being reachable by an agent fails behind it.

```csharp
public static void AllowPreReleasePackages()
```

### ImportSamples() {#importsamples}

Imports the XR samples the framework's prefabs and scenes are built on. The installed
package list is read synchronously here; the old setup asked the package manager for it
asynchronously and then raced its own callback.

```csharp
public static void ImportSamples()
```

### ImportTextMeshProResources() {#importtextmeshproresources}

Imports the TextMesh Pro essential resources, without which every piece of text in the
framework's prefabs renders as a magenta box. Skipped when they are already there.
The Examples & Extras package is deliberately not imported. Nothing in the framework or
in a project built on it references any of its assets, so all it ever did was put demo
scenes, prefabs and scripts into every project.
